pathway.title: B&G Foods, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage and cover are the binding weakness. Net debt is 6.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and 15.00x reported EBITDA at the latest quarter end, and twelve-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid 2.08x, with reported EBITDA at 0.96x. Pro forma for the October 13, 2026 sale of the B&M and Joan of Arc brands, net leverage on reported EBITDA is 14.93x, and 15.05x after the October 30, 2026 dividend; the issuer-adjusted pro forma is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K3

- The interest burden is rising after the June 2026 refinancing. At October 3, 2026 balances and printed rates, contractual cash interest is $169.74 million a year, $32.69 million more than the cash interest paid over the twelve months, which takes cover on issuer-adjusted EBITDA to 1.68x. The credit agreement sets a minimum interest cover of 1.75x on its own definitions, which the filings do not reproduce, so headroom is not established, but the two measures are close enough that the definitions are the first document to obtain. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation K4; calculation K5

- Liquidity is thin and shrinking at the seasonal peak. Revolver availability fell from $207.6 million at the end of fiscal 2025 to $55.1 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026, and cash plus availability totals $116.84 million at that date, with the pro forma effect on cash of the October 13, 2026 brand sale and the October 30, 2026 dividend not established, while the issuer says its liquidity needs are greatest from June to October. No bond matures before September 2028, so the risk is a squeeze on liquidity rather than a near-term maturity. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-04-04_bgs_bgs-20260404x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation K6

- Refinancing capacity decides the outcome. $1,157.69 million falls due in fiscal 2028, made up of the revolver, the 2028 secured notes and term loan amortization, and the first of them, the 2028 secured notes, matures 667 days from the as-of date; $432.0 million of term loans follow in 2029. The 2031 notes priced at 97.67% of face value with an 11.00% coupon, which shows market access at a high cost, and secured principal is 5.61x issuer-adjusted EBITDA against a 4.00x test for incremental secured debt on the credit agreement's own definitions, so new secured capacity is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K7; calculation K13

- The base business is the main support. Base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 after falling 4.0% in fiscal 2025, helped by volume growth of 1.4%, which gives some cash-flow visibility if the turn lasts. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation K14

- The quality of earnings is weaker than the headline. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose 6.59% over the nine months, but it adds back $32,427 thousand of acquisition, divestiture-related and non-recurring costs against $9,993 thousand a year earlier, and after deducting them earnings fell 5.67%. The largest segment's adjusted EBITDA fell 19.4%, mainly on higher oil and diesel costs, and the gain came from the smaller Spices & Flavor Solutions segment, the sale of the near break-even Frozen business and lower tariff expense that includes refunds, which may not repeat. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K17

- Cash conversion is adequate on paper and weak after dividends. Capital expenditure is low and twelve-month free cash flow was 34.96% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA, but a large rise in trade payables lifted it and can reverse, and free cash flow fell short of dividends by $26.53 million in the first three quarters of 2026, most of which were paid before the cut took effect. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 67–69; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K8

- Margin resilience depends on pricing catching up with costs. The issuer says price increases and savings have not fully offset cost increases in recent years, it is locked into supply and prices for most key raw materials only through the end of fiscal 2026, and it expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63

- Financial policy has turned more creditor-friendly, but governance leaves open questions. The dividend rate was halved, which saves about $29.8 million a year, no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, and the chief executive retired in August 2026 with no successor named in the supplied text. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K15

- Brand values and sales scale keep eroding. Net sales fell 5.4% in fiscal 2025, mainly on lower base business sales, and 2.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, mostly through disposals; intangible impairments recurred, and market capitalization stood below book equity at the latest quarter end. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

cells.text: Manufactures, sells and distributes branded shelf-stable and frozen food and household products in the United States, Canada and Puerto Rico, and also sells private label and foodservice products; management says many brands hold leading regional or national shares [Management Language]

Four segments. Fiscal 2025 net sales of $1,828.7 million: Specialty 34.45%, Meals 24.30%, Frozen & Vegetables 19.61%, Spices & Flavor Solutions 21.64%. First three quarters of 2026 net sales of $1,252.0 million: 33.77%, 28.61%, 13.79% and 23.83% (calculations A2 and A3)

Walmart took 31.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales and 28.9% in the first three quarters of 2026; the ten largest customers took 63.6% and 59.3%; Walmart buys from all four segments and held 28.9% of trade receivables at October 3, 2026 (39.0% at January 3, 2026)

Sales to foreign customers, mainly in Canada, were 9.1% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and 13.4% in the first three quarters of 2026; long-lived assets outside the United States were 6.6% of the total at October 3, 2026

Supermarkets, mass merchants, warehouse clubs, wholesalers, foodservice, drug and dollar stores and e-tailers, sold directly and through brokers; six shelf-stable and seven frozen distribution centres, mostly run by third-party logistics providers, with the frozen centres transitioning to the acquirers of the Green Giant businesses

Ten manufacturing facilities (six owned, two leased, two mixed); a significant part of the products is made under co-packing arrangements; a co-manufacturing agreement with Seneca Foods at Irapuato, Mexico supplied $58.7 million of net sales in the first three quarters of 2026

Corn, peas, broccoli, oils, beans, spices, maple syrup, wheat, nuts, tomatoes, sugar and packaging; Green Giant vegetables are bought under dedicated acreage contracts; costs were elevated in fiscal 2023 to 2025 and are expected to stay elevated in fiscal 2026; the issuer says price increases and savings have not fully offset cost increases [Management Language]; tariffs touch spices and steel cans
Gross profit was 21.8% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and 21.4% in the first three quarters of 2026; adjusted gross profit was 22.0% and 22.3% against 21.6% a year earlier (calculation A12)

Sales are higher in the first and fourth quarters; produce is bought from June to October and maple syrup from April to August, when liquidity needs are greatest; inventories were $424.6 million at October 3, 2026, plus $70.2 million of inventories held for sale
Capital expenditures were $30.6 million in fiscal 2025 and $17.8 million in the first three quarters of 2026, with $25.0 million or less planned for fiscal 2026

2,497 employees at January 3, 2026, of whom 2,085 were in manufacturing; 48.3% were covered by collective bargaining agreements, and the Terre Haute and Cincinnati agreements expire on March 30, 2027 and April 30, 2027; four company pension plans cover 21.4% of employees (calculation A13)

Acquisition-led since 1996: more than 50 brands acquired in the fiscal 2025 annual report and more than 45 in the latest quarterly report; the stated strategy now pairs bolt-on acquisitions with divestitures to sharpen focus, improve margins and reduce long-term debt [Management Language]
Competes with larger and less leveraged companies and with private label; traditional centre-of-store grocery brands have often had flat to modestly declining sales [Management Language]

runs.text: Strengths. The base business has stopped shrinking: base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 on volume growth of 1.4% after a 4.0% fall in fiscal 2025, which supports cash-flow visibility if it lasts. Capital intensity is low and policy has tightened: capital expenditure was $17.8 million in the first three quarters of 2026 and the dividend rate was halved, so more of each dollar of operating cash flow stays in the business. The 2031 notes cleared the 2027 maturity, so no bond matures before September 2028 and refinancing risk sits about two years away. Four segments and many brands spread sales, with no segment above 34.45% of net sales in fiscal 2025, which limits dependence on any one product line. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 144–145; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14; calculation K15

Weaknesses. Leverage is near seven times issuer-adjusted EBITDA and cover is about two times before the full-year cost of the 2031 notes, which leaves little room for an earnings shortfall. Revolver availability fell to $55.1 million from $207.6 million in nine months, so liquidity is the first thing to give in a downturn or a seasonal build. The $1,157.69 million of fiscal 2028 maturities must be refinanced after covenant step-downs in 2027, and the June 2026 financing cost an 11.00% coupon. One retailer takes 31.0% of net sales, and the largest segment's adjusted EBITDA fell 19.4% on input and logistics costs, so margin is exposed where concentration is highest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation K3; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K7

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Since May 2025 the issuer has sold four brand groups and bought one. The Don Pepino and Sclafani brands (May 23, 2025, $10.6 million), the Le Sueur brand in the United States (August 1, 2025, $59.1 million), the Green Giant frozen business in the United States (March 2, 2026, about $61.5 million, with a continuing co-manufacturing agreement) and the B&M and Joan of Arc brands (October 13, 2026, $8.0 million, after the quarter end) were sold. The College Inn and Kitchen Basics broth brands were bought on March 19, 2026 for $109.7 million in cash, after an agreement dated January 15, 2026. The issuer says the purpose is to sharpen focus, improve margins and reduce long-term debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 112

A sale of the Green Giant business in Canada to Nortera Foods, agreed on October 24, 2025 at inventory value plus $5.0 million (about $60.0 million on September 27, 2025 inventory), was terminated by mutual agreement on October 5, 2026 because Canadian competition approval had not been obtained by September 24, 2026. The issuer still classifies the assets as held for sale ($52.9 million at October 3, 2026), says it continues to pursue a sale and believes one is probable within a year; no buyer or price is stated. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39

On June 10, 2026 the issuer sold $475.0 million of 11.00% senior notes due 2031 at 97.67% of face value. The notes are unsecured, are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries, pay interest each June 15 and December 15 from December 15, 2026, and can be called at 105.50% from June 15, 2028. With revolver borrowings and cash, the proceeds redeemed all $509.3 million of the 5.25% senior notes due 2027 at par, with the redemption date July 4, 2026 and payment on July 6, 2026, after the second-quarter balance-sheet date, and a $1.1 million loss on extinguishment. Debt financing costs paid in the first three quarters of 2026 were $18.4 million against $0.9 million a year earlier, and the issuer borrowed $180.0 million and repaid $40.0 million under the revolver. The 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 ($799.3 million outstanding) rank equally with the credit agreement and ahead of the new unsecured notes to the extent of the collateral. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A15

Earlier debt actions set the structure. The issuer sold $550.0 million of the 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 on September 26, 2023 at 99.502% of face value and a further $250.0 million on July 12, 2024 at 100.5%, when it also cut the term loans from $507.3 million to $450.0 million with maturity extended to October 2029 and cut revolver capacity from $800.0 million to $475.0 million, and redeemed the $265.4 million of 5.25% notes due 2025 on October 9, 2024 with revolver loans and cash. On July 1, 2025 the credit agreement was amended to cut revolver commitments from $475.0 million to $430.0 million and to raise the maximum leverage ratio temporarily, for a $0.8 million fee. During 2025 the issuer also bought $20.7 million (second quarter) and $20.0 million (third quarter) of the 2027 notes in the open market at 89.98% and 96.00% of face value. The supplied filings state at-the-market equity sales of $66.6 million gross in fiscal 2022 and $75.3 million gross in fiscal 2023, with the net proceeds used to repay, redeem or repurchase long-term debt, pay offering costs and for general corporate purposes, and none in fiscal 2024; the cash flow statements show no stock issuance proceeds in fiscal 2025 or the first three quarters of 2026. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-28_bgs_bgs-20241228x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 118–119; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 119–122; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 123–124; 10-K_2024-12-28_bgs_bgs-20241228x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8

fields.value: Cover is thin: issuer-adjusted EBITDA is 2.08x cash interest and reported EBITDA is only 0.96x, before the full-year cost of the 11.00% notes that replaced the 5.25% notes. Undrawn revolver capacity net of letters of credit has fallen to USD 55.1 million from USD 207.6 million at the end of fiscal 2025, and borrowings and asset sales, not operating cash, funded the 2026 acquisition and dividends. Debt maturities are concentrated in 2028, and the twelve-month figures span 53 weeks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose by USD 84,328 thousand in the 39 weeks to October 3, 2026, to USD 1,978,111 thousand, because the USD 109,655 thousand acquisition of the College Inn and Kitchen Basics brands and USD 38,341 thousand of dividends outran USD 61,437 thousand of asset sale proceeds and USD 29,566 thousand of operating cash flow. The consequence is that deleveraging now depends on further disposals and cost savings rather than on cash generation. The revolver's maximum leverage ratio steps down from 7.50x to 7.25x for the quarter ending January 2, 2027 and to 7.00x from April 3, 2027, but headroom is not established because the covenant's own EBITDA and net debt definitions are not reproduced in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross leverage on reported EBITDA is 11.60x for fiscal 2025 and 15.46x for the twelve months to October 3, 2026, but reported EBITDA is depressed by non-cash impairments and by the loss on the Green Giant frozen sale, which the issuer adds back; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA the same ratios are 7.16x and 7.17x. The strongest contrary reading is that the add-backs are largely non-cash, which would make the adjusted ratio the better guide to debt service; against that, impairments in fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and again in the third quarter of 2026, with reported EBITDA negative in fiscal 2024, show an asset base losing value, so the adjusted ratio may understate the risk that brand values cannot support the debt in a sale or restructuring.

After capital expenditures of USD 17,752 thousand, free cash flow was USD 11,814 thousand, well below the USD 38,341 thousand of dividends paid; the issuer has since halved its dividend rate and drew on the revolver to fund the shortfall, which is a direct claim on liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: B&G Foods, Inc. (issuer bgs-1278027), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, transaction, ownership, governance and operating model facts that matter to a creditor, taken from the five supplied filings with the source readiness answer as context.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors should treat B&G Foods as a shrinking-sales, customer-concentrated branded-food credit that is reshaping its portfolio and has accepted a much higher coupon to move its nearest bond maturity to September 2028, with no identified sponsor to support or drain it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The portfolio changes since 2025 trade a lower-margin frozen business and small shelf-stable brands for higher-margin broth brands, and the board halved the dividend rate, which reduces cash leakage. The open questions are who leads the company after the chief executive's retirement in August 2026 and who holds the shares, because the successor and the proxy statement are not in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is the operating fact that matters most for cash-flow stability: one retailer, Walmart, took 31.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales and the ten largest customers took 63.6%, so one negotiation on price, promotions or shelf space can move a large part of earnings. The retailer's share eased to 28.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, and it held about the same share of trade receivables at the quarter end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sales base is shrinking through disposals while the underlying brands have stopped declining. Net sales fell 5.4% in fiscal 2025 and 2.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, but base business net sales, which exclude acquired and divested brands, rose 1.8% in 2026 after falling 4.0% in fiscal 2025, helped by volume growth of 1.4%. Creditors are relying on mix and cost recovery, not growth, for cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The June 2026 refinancing bought time at a high price and did not fund itself. The $475.0 million of 11.00% notes due 2031 replaced $509.3 million of 5.25% notes due 2027, which lifts the annual coupon on those principal amounts by $25.51 million. The new notes raised $463.9 million at their issue price, $45.4 million less than the redemption amount, so cash and the revolver covered the gap, and net revolver borrowings were $140.0 million over the first three quarters of 2026. The nearest bond maturity moved from September 2027 to September 2028, but revolver availability fell to $55.1 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026 from $207.6 million at the end of fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disposals have raised modest cash and have not reduced debt. The four brand sales completed since May 2025 carried stated prices totalling $139.2 million against $109.7 million paid for the College Inn and Kitchen Basics brands, yet principal debt outstanding at the latest quarter end was $26.0 million higher than at the end of fiscal 2024. Three of the four sales came with a loss on sale or a preceding impairment, so the programme has so far reshaped the portfolio more than it has repaid debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation A6; calculation A7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Brand values keep being marked down, which signals lower expected cash flows from the affected brands. Intangible impairments were $320.0 million in fiscal 2024 (with a $70.6 million goodwill impairment), $60.8 million in fiscal 2025 and $40.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, while market capitalization stood below book equity at the latest quarter end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation A10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is dispersed public equity with no controlling holder identified, so there is no sponsor to lean on, and the supplied filings state no sponsor fees, related-party payments or sponsor-led recapitalisation, only covenant limits on dealings with affiliates. The documents that would name large holders were not supplied, so this rests on absence of evidence and could change with one document.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dividend cut is the clearest creditor-friendly decision of the period, but it stays at the board's discretion. The rate was halved to $0.38 per share per annum from the payment declared in May 2026, which takes expected dividends to $30.8 million in fiscal 2027 from $60.6 million paid in fiscal 2025, after dividends exceeded operating cash flow in the first three quarters of both 2025 and 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The chief executive's retirement lands in the middle of the refinancing and disposal programme, and the supplied filings do not say who succeeds. Separation costs of $5.3 million were recorded in the third quarter against $4.5 million expected a quarter earlier, and the chief executive is the issuer's decision maker for segment resource allocation, so who holds the role matters for the portfolio plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation A9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating model is seasonal and working-capital heavy, so the third quarter is when liquidity is tightest. The issuer buys most produce from June to October and most maple syrup from April to August, says its liquidity needs are greatest in those months, and had $55.1 million of revolver availability at the end of the third quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the underlying business has stopped shrinking and is earning more on what is left. Base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 on volume growth of 1.4%, adjusted gross profit was 22.3% of net sales against 21.6% a year earlier as higher-margin broth brands joined, a lower-margin frozen business left and tariff expense fell, and the issuer reports compliance with every covenant at the latest quarter end. The 2031 notes also remove the 2027 maturity, so no bond matures before September 2028, and the halved dividend keeps roughly $29.8 million a year inside the business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation A8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three developments would turn the view more constructive: a named chief executive with a stated plan for the disposal programme, a completed sale of the Green Giant Canada business with proceeds applied to the revolver, and a proxy statement showing a large holder committed to the equity. Three would turn it more negative: base business net sales falling again, a further failed or discounted disposal, and a change in terms from the largest customer. A covenant ratio close to its limit would also change the view, but the supplied filings do not print the ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The conclusion that no sponsor is present rests on the absence of a named large holder in the supplied filings; the proxy statement and any ownership filings were not supplied, so a controlling or activist holder could exist and would change the ownership reading from dispersed to concentrated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The leadership finding covers only the retirement terms: the successor, any interim arrangement and any change of plan are not stated in the supplied text, so the execution risk could be higher or lower than described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The transaction findings rest on the issuer's own summaries; the purchase agreements, the indentures and the credit agreement were not supplied, so what the issuer may still sell, pay out or borrow is not established and the disposal and distribution conclusions are directional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is sized by share of sales and receivables only; contract terms, rebates and promotion commitments with the largest customer are not disclosed, so the severity of the single-buyer risk cannot be quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest quarterly filing is eight days before the as-of date, so a later sale, financing or management announcement would change the timeline and the transaction findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The margin comparison in the contrary evidence uses the issuer's own adjusted measure, which is not audited, so the improvement is directional rather than exact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Since May 2025 the issuer has sold four brand groups and bought one. The Don Pepino and Sclafani brands (May 23, 2025, $10.6 million), the Le Sueur brand in the United States (August 1, 2025, $59.1 million), the Green Giant frozen business in the United States (March 2, 2026, about $61.5 million, with a continuing co-manufacturing agreement) and the B&M and Joan of Arc brands (October 13, 2026, $8.0 million, after the quarter end) were sold. The College Inn and Kitchen Basics broth brands were bought on March 19, 2026 for $109.7 million in cash, after an agreement dated January 15, 2026. The issuer says the purpose is to sharpen focus, improve margins and reduce long-term debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A sale of the Green Giant business in Canada to Nortera Foods, agreed on October 24, 2025 at inventory value plus $5.0 million (about $60.0 million on September 27, 2025 inventory), was terminated by mutual agreement on October 5, 2026 because Canadian competition approval had not been obtained by September 24, 2026. The issuer still classifies the assets as held for sale ($52.9 million at October 3, 2026), says it continues to pursue a sale and believes one is probable within a year; no buyer or price is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On June 10, 2026 the issuer sold $475.0 million of 11.00% senior notes due 2031 at 97.67% of face value. The notes are unsecured, are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries, pay interest each June 15 and December 15 from December 15, 2026, and can be called at 105.50% from June 15, 2028. With revolver borrowings and cash, the proceeds redeemed all $509.3 million of the 5.25% senior notes due 2027 at par, with the redemption date July 4, 2026 and payment on July 6, 2026, after the second-quarter balance-sheet date, and a $1.1 million loss on extinguishment. Debt financing costs paid in the first three quarters of 2026 were $18.4 million against $0.9 million a year earlier, and the issuer borrowed $180.0 million and repaid $40.0 million under the revolver. The 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 ($799.3 million outstanding) rank equally with the credit agreement and ahead of the new unsecured notes to the extent of the collateral.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 22–25; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation A4; calculation A5; calculation A15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier debt actions set the structure. The issuer sold $550.0 million of the 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 on September 26, 2023 at 99.502% of face value and a further $250.0 million on July 12, 2024 at 100.5%, when it also cut the term loans from $507.3 million to $450.0 million with maturity extended to October 2029 and cut revolver capacity from $800.0 million to $475.0 million, and redeemed the $265.4 million of 5.25% notes due 2025 on October 9, 2024 with revolver loans and cash. On July 1, 2025 the credit agreement was amended to cut revolver commitments from $475.0 million to $430.0 million and to raise the maximum leverage ratio temporarily, for a $0.8 million fee. During 2025 the issuer also bought $20.7 million (second quarter) and $20.0 million (third quarter) of the 2027 notes in the open market at 89.98% and 96.00% of face value. The supplied filings state at-the-market equity sales of $66.6 million gross in fiscal 2022 and $75.3 million gross in fiscal 2023, with the net proceeds used to repay, redeem or repurchase long-term debt, pay offering costs and for general corporate purposes, and none in fiscal 2024; the cash flow statements show no stock issuance proceeds in fiscal 2025 or the first three quarters of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by distributions that exceeded operating cash flow before the 2026 cut, debt that rose while the portfolio was reshaped and a leadership transition under way, because they weaken liquidity and add execution risk, which implies more reliance on refinancing access. Countervailing evidence is the halved dividend, the extended maturity, regular and audited reporting, compliance with covenants and the absence of any creditor-adverse transaction in the supplied filings. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the report on Form 8-K filed August 11, 2026.

fields.value: B&G Foods, Inc. (issuer bgs-1278027), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit profile: business quality, financial profile, refinancing capacity, the primary downside path and monitoring triggers, built on the five supplied filings and the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance answers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors should treat B&G Foods as a highly leveraged, thinly covered branded-food credit whose steady base business can service debt to 2028 only if liquidity is not drawn down further and the 2028 maturities are refinanced; refinancing, not operations, decides the outcome.

fields.value: - The interest burden is rising after the June 2026 refinancing. At October 3, 2026 balances and printed rates, contractual cash interest is $169.74 million a year, $32.69 million more than the cash interest paid over the twelve months, which takes cover on issuer-adjusted EBITDA to 1.68x. The credit agreement sets a minimum interest cover of 1.75x on its own definitions, which the filings do not reproduce, so headroom is not established, but the two measures are close enough that the definitions are the first document to obtain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation K4; calculation K5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is thin and shrinking at the seasonal peak. Revolver availability fell from $207.6 million at the end of fiscal 2025 to $55.1 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026, and cash plus availability totals $116.84 million at that date, with the pro forma effect on cash of the October 13, 2026 brand sale and the October 30, 2026 dividend not established, while the issuer says its liquidity needs are greatest from June to October. No bond matures before September 2028, so the risk is a squeeze on liquidity rather than a near-term maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-04-04_bgs_bgs-20260404x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation K6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing capacity decides the outcome. $1,157.69 million falls due in fiscal 2028, made up of the revolver, the 2028 secured notes and term loan amortization, and the first of them, the 2028 secured notes, matures 667 days from the as-of date; $432.0 million of term loans follow in 2029. The 2031 notes priced at 97.67% of face value with an 11.00% coupon, which shows market access at a high cost, and secured principal is 5.61x issuer-adjusted EBITDA against a 4.00x test for incremental secured debt on the credit agreement's own definitions, so new secured capacity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K7; calculation K13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The base business is the main support. Base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 after falling 4.0% in fiscal 2025, helped by volume growth of 1.4%, which gives some cash-flow visibility if the turn lasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The quality of earnings is weaker than the headline. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose 6.59% over the nine months, but it adds back $32,427 thousand of acquisition, divestiture-related and non-recurring costs against $9,993 thousand a year earlier, and after deducting them earnings fell 5.67%. The largest segment's adjusted EBITDA fell 19.4%, mainly on higher oil and diesel costs, and the gain came from the smaller Spices & Flavor Solutions segment, the sale of the near break-even Frozen business and lower tariff expense that includes refunds, which may not repeat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is adequate on paper and weak after dividends. Capital expenditure is low and twelve-month free cash flow was 34.96% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA, but a large rise in trade payables lifted it and can reverse, and free cash flow fell short of dividends by $26.53 million in the first three quarters of 2026, most of which were paid before the cut took effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 67–69; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin resilience depends on pricing catching up with costs. The issuer says price increases and savings have not fully offset cost increases in recent years, it is locked into supply and prices for most key raw materials only through the end of fiscal 2026, and it expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy has turned more creditor-friendly, but governance leaves open questions. The dividend rate was halved, which saves about $29.8 million a year, no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, and the chief executive retired in August 2026 with no successor named in the supplied text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Brand values and sales scale keep eroding. Net sales fell 5.4% in fiscal 2025, mainly on lower base business sales, and 2.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, mostly through disposals; intangible impairments recurred, and market capitalization stood below book equity at the latest quarter end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the cautious reading is that issuer-adjusted figures may be the better guide to debt service, because 71.43% of the add-backs in the first nine months of 2026 were non-cash write-downs and losses on sales, which would make leverage near seven times a truer burden than fifteen times, although the acquisition, divestiture-related and non-recurring costs among the add-backs more than tripled. The base business has returned to volume growth, the dividend is halved, capital expenditure is planned at $25.0 million or less, no bond matures before September 2028, and assets held for sale of $52.9 million, mostly Canadian inventory that the issuer still means to sell, are a liquidity source that is not yet agreed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 69–70; calculation K1; calculation K17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three developments would turn the view more constructive: two or more further quarters of base business growth with the largest segment's margin recovering, revolver availability rebuilt above the $140.1 million seen on April 4, 2026, and the 2028 maturities refinanced early. Four would turn it more negative: base business net sales turning down again, the largest segment's adjusted EBITDA falling further, availability dropping below the $55.1 million of October 3, 2026, and issuer-adjusted leverage moving toward the covenant step-downs of 7.25x and 7.00x, whose headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The conclusion that leverage and cover are the binding weakness uses the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA and printed cash interest; the credit agreement's EBITDA and interest definitions are not reproduced, so any reading against the covenant levels is an approximation and covenant headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The run-rate interest burden holds October 3, 2026 balances and floating rates unchanged and leaves out fees and non-cash amortization, so the cover of 1.68x could prove higher or lower.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside scenario rests on a ratio of lost earnings to lost sales observed over only two annual periods, so its leverage and cover results are illustrations of direction and size, not forecasts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management guidance for sales or earnings, no credit ratings and no market prices are in the supplied documents, so the outlook is qualitative and the business profile cannot be benchmarked against other leveraged food issuers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The twelve-month figures span 53 weeks and mix two add-back definitions, which flatters leverage and cover slightly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The base business has stopped shrinking: base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 on volume growth of 1.4% after a 4.0% fall in fiscal 2025, which supports cash-flow visibility if it lasts. Capital intensity is low and policy has tightened: capital expenditure was $17.8 million in the first three quarters of 2026 and the dividend rate was halved, so more of each dollar of operating cash flow stays in the business. The 2031 notes cleared the 2027 maturity, so no bond matures before September 2028 and refinancing risk sits about two years away. Four segments and many brands spread sales, with no segment above 34.45% of net sales in fiscal 2025, which limits dependence on any one product line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 144–145; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14; calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage is near seven times issuer-adjusted EBITDA and cover is about two times before the full-year cost of the 2031 notes, which leaves little room for an earnings shortfall. Revolver availability fell to $55.1 million from $207.6 million in nine months, so liquidity is the first thing to give in a downturn or a seasonal build. The $1,157.69 million of fiscal 2028 maturities must be refinanced after covenant step-downs in 2027, and the June 2026 financing cost an 11.00% coupon. One retailer takes 31.0% of net sales, and the largest segment's adjusted EBITDA fell 19.4% on input and logistics costs, so margin is exposed where concentration is highest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation K3; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: B&G Foods sells branded shelf-stable and frozen food and household products, mostly in the United States, through four segments, and its cash flow rests on long-established brands in categories the issuer itself describes as often flat to modestly declining. The portfolio is being reshaped: four brand sales since May 2025 and one acquisition have lowered reported net sales while the issuer says they raise margin. Revenue visibility is moderate because the products are staples bought through large retailers, but concentration is high, with one customer at 31.0% of net sales and contract terms not disclosed. For creditors the business supports steady, low-growth cash flow that can service debt only while costs and retailer terms stay stable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a listed holding company whose domestic subsidiaries guarantee its debt, while foreign subsidiaries do not guarantee the 2031 notes. Ownership is dispersed and no sponsor or controlling holder is identified in the supplied filings, although the proxy statement that would show large holders was not supplied. The board sets financial policy: the stated policy distributes a substantial portion of available cash, the dividend rate was halved in 2026 and the board can change it at any time. The chief executive retired in August 2026 with no successor named in the supplied text. For creditors this means no sponsor support or sponsor extraction to weigh, a dividend that is a policy choice rather than a covenant-forced one, and an open leadership question.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net sales fell 6.30% in fiscal 2024 and 5.37% in fiscal 2025, which the issuer states as 5.4% and attributes mainly to lower base business sales, and 2.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, mostly through divestitures. Base business net sales fell 4.0% in fiscal 2025 on volume down 3.5% and price and mix down 0.3%, and rose 1.8% in 2026 on volume up 1.4% and price and mix up 0.3%. Pricing power is limited: the issuer says price increases may lag costs and competition can limit quick increases, retailers push for lower prices and more promotion and favour private label, and part of the Spices & Flavor Solutions growth came from private label and foodservice. Revenue is therefore predictable as staple demand but structurally pressured by channel shifts and concentrated in one buyer, so creditors can lean on the 2026 volume turn only if it persists for several quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation K14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross profit was 21.8% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and 21.4% in the first three quarters of 2026, so small cost movements matter, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 15.88% of net sales over the twelve months against 14.88% in fiscal 2025 and 15.29% in fiscal 2024. Inputs are agricultural products, oils, packaging and freight; the issuer is locked into supply and prices for most key raw materials only through the end of fiscal 2026 and expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027. The largest segment shows the pressure: Specialty adjusted EBITDA fell 19.4% over nine months on higher oil input costs for Crisco and diesel-driven logistics costs, while Spices & Flavor Solutions rose 21.9% on pricing, lower spice costs and lower tariff expense that includes refunds; the Don Pepino sale also played a small part in the Specialty fall. Margins can be defended only where pricing catches up with costs, and part of the group improvement is one-off, so margin stability is average at best.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 65; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K9; calculation K10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure is low, $30.6 million in fiscal 2025 and $17.8 million in the first three quarters of 2026, with $25.0 million or less planned for fiscal 2026, and the business is seasonal, buying produce from June to October and maple syrup from April to August. Twelve-month free cash flow was 34.96% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA, but a large rise in trade payables lifted operating cash flow and can reverse, and acquisition, divestiture-related and non-recurring costs recur while the portfolio is reshaped: the amount added back to issuer-adjusted EBITDA was $32,427 thousand in the first three quarters of 2026 against $9,993 thousand a year earlier, which is largely cash leaving the business. Cash interest is the largest fixed claim and is rising, because the 2031 notes replaced lower-cost notes and the first coupon on them falls due on December 15, 2026. Cash conversion is adequate before dividends and weak after them, which is why the dividend cut matters to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 67–70; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K4; calculation K8; calculation K17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense: the issuer competes with numerous companies, including larger and less leveraged ones, and with private label, so margin depends on brand strength in each category. Buyer power is the strongest force, with one retailer at 31.0% of net sales, ten customers at 63.6% and consolidating retailers demanding lower prices and more promotion. Supplier power is moderate: inputs are commodities bought under short contracts or advance purchases, Green Giant vegetables come under dedicated acreage contracts and a significant part of production is outsourced to co-packers who serve other companies. The threat of substitutes comes from private label and alternative outlets such as warehouse clubs, dollar stores and e-commerce, and the threat of new entrants is not quantified in the supplied filings. For creditors the forces cap pricing power and make volume the main lever for earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trade policy and fuel costs are the factors that alter credit quality. Tariffs on imported spices and steel cans raised costs, tariff refunds followed a February 2026 court ruling and some may have to be shared with customers, and retaliation could hurt sales in Canada. Diesel and freight costs rose in 2026 and the issuer expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027. Social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the supplied materials, apart from the shift toward e-commerce and private label already counted under competition. For creditors the tariff refund is a non-recurring gain to earnings and fuel costs are a recurring margin risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are established brands with stabilising volumes, low capital intensity, a halved dividend and no bond maturity before September 2028. Weaknesses are leverage near seven times issuer-adjusted EBITDA, thin cover, a shrinking revolver cushion, one customer at 31.0% of net sales and a largest segment whose earnings are falling. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a completed sale of the Green Giant Canada business with proceeds applied to the revolver, continued base business volume growth and pricing that catches up with costs. Threats that could weaken it are cost inflation in oil and fuel, retailer demands for price and promotion, tariff changes and the covenant step-downs in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: net sales of $1,791.549 million over twelve months are falling, through lower base sales in fiscal 2025 and disposals in 2026, and the issuer's category leadership claims cannot be benchmarked because no peer data was supplied. Competitive advantage is average, resting on brands the issuer calls leaders in their categories but under retailer and private-label pressure. Business diversification is average, with four segments but one dominant customer. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low and the dividend has been cut, but the split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed and the issuer has not yet priced through input costs. Margin stability is weak to average, with the largest segment's earnings falling and group gains partly one-off. Free cash flow stability is weak, since cash flow falls short of dividends in the first three quarters of both 2025 and 2026 and rising interest absorbs more. The ability to refinance is average to weak, with market access shown at a high cost and $1,157.69 million due in fiscal 2028. Liquidity is weak, with $116.84 million of cash and availability at October 3, 2026, the seasonal peak. Financial policy and governance are average, with a creditor-friendlier dividend but a leadership change and no identified owner. The trend is stabilising operations against deteriorating liquidity and coverage, and the key missing data points are the covenant calculation and the credit agreement definitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation K3; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are base business volume growth, a dividend cost of $30.8 million a year in fiscal 2027, capital expenditure of $25.0 million or less, supply and prices locked for most key materials through the end of fiscal 2026 and a possible sale of the Green Giant Canada business. The headwinds are the first full year of the 2031 notes, with the first coupon due on December 15, 2026, freight elevated into fiscal 2027, labour agreements at two Specialty plants expiring on March 30 and April 30, 2027, covenant step-downs on January 2 and April 3, 2027 and the leadership transition. Over three to five years the issue is refinancing the 2028 maturities with covenants tighter and a portfolio smaller than today. The supplied filings give no guidance for sales or earnings, so these items are directional and carry no forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 69–70; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario replays the issuer's own fiscal 2025 experience. The initiating condition is a retailer or category setback that cuts net sales by 5.37%, the fall seen in fiscal 2025, from the twelve-month level of $1,791.549 million. The first operational break is lost volume with costs for oil, fuel and freight still rising, and in fiscal 2025 each dollar of lost net sales coincided with 22.37 cents of lost issuer-adjusted EBITDA. On that ratio net sales fall $96.20 million and issuer-adjusted EBITDA falls $21.52 million to $263.04 million, which takes net debt to 7.52x issuer-adjusted EBITDA from 6.95x and cover on run-rate interest to 1.55x from 1.68x. Free cash flow falls by about the lost earnings before tax while cash interest steps up to its run-rate of $169.74 million, so the seasonal build would rely on $55.1 million of revolver availability. Management levers are the remaining dividend of $30.8 million a year, capital expenditure of $25.0 million or less, inventory release and a sale of the Canadian business. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months, because no bond matures before September 2028, but the covenant step-downs to 7.25x and 7.00x would be the first break and cannot be tested here, and a covenant breach would put the 2028 refinancing at risk. The observable triggers are base business net sales, Specialty adjusted EBITDA, revolver availability and the compliance statements in each quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 81; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 69–70; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K4; calculation K5; calculation K11; calculation K12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, B&G Foods presents an adequate business profile supported by established brands with stabilising volumes, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover and a narrow revolver cushion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate before dividends and weak after them, because capital expenditure is low but cash interest is rising and cash flow has fallen short of dividends. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on base business growth, the largest segment's margin recovering, liquidity being rebuilt and covenant room being shown before the 2028 maturities become current. The primary downside path is renewed sales and margin pressure in the largest segment feeding a covenant step-down in 2027 and a harder 2028 refinancing.
